FREE PRINTABLE / HEART ANATOMY

Color it. Label it. Recall it.

Coloring is more useful when your brain has to do some work. Use this one-page activity to trace the two blood routes, name the chambers and valves, then rebuild the pathway without looking.

Print at 100% on US Letter paper.
Answer key is on the lesson page.

Review the full blood-flow lesson first
ACTIVITY SHEET / 001COLOR KEY

Color by oxygen route.

Blue: oxygen-poor blood on its way from the body to the lungs.
Red: oxygen-rich blood on its way from the lungs to the body.

ONE-PAGE PRACTICEColor the routeLabel 4 chambersRecall 4 valves

01 / How to use the page

Try before you check.

First, use two colors to trace the route: body to right heart to lungs, then lungs to left heart to body. Next, label the four chambers inside the diagram and write the valve names beside the arrows.

Cover the completed labels and say the full pathway aloud. The blank page turns familiar shapes into retrieval practice instead of passive decoration.

Color key: the colors are a teaching convention, not the actual color of blood. Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood toward it.

02 / Why answer first?

Make the page work for memory.

  1. Retrieve

    Try the labels and pathway before reopening the lesson.

  2. Check

    Compare your answer with the explanation; correct the exact point that broke the route.

  3. Repeat

    Leave a little time, then redraw the pathway from a blank page.

03 / One quick answer check

Did you put the sides in order?

Use the full lesson if anything
in the sequence feels uncertain.

What are the four chambers in flow order?

Right atrium → right ventricle → left atrium → left ventricle. The lungs sit between the right ventricle and left atrium.

Which four valve names belong on the diagram?

Tricuspid, pulmonary semilunar, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic semilunar. They separate the chambers and the two ventricular outflow routes.
